meetings.title: H2 Product Strategy & AI Memory Architecture

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Thanks everyone for hopping on. Today we need to align on our H2 product strategy, specifically our transition to proactive AI meeting intelligence and accountability auditing.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: From the infrastructure side, we completed the serverless PostgreSQL migration with Neon. Sub-50ms query latency for full-text search across transcripts is now rock solid.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Brody
transcript.text: For the AI models, we benchmarked GPT-4o Mini against Claude 3.5 Sonnet. For transcript summary generation and gap auditing, 4o-mini gives us a 92% cost reduction with virtually identical extraction quality.

transcript.speaker: Elena Rostova
transcript.text: User testing showed that executives don't just want bullet points—they want to see 'Readiness Scores' and click directly on timeline moments where unassigned blockers were mentioned.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: That's a huge point. Let's make sure the AI Review tab is front and center. I want unresolved questions and unassigned commitments highlighted immediately after any call finishes.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: We should also implement JSON meeting export and import so customers can easily back up their workspaces and import legacy meeting records.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Brody
transcript.text: Agreed. I will finalize the prompt templates for risk audits and test edge cases like contradictory stakeholder deadlines.

transcript.speaker: Elena Rostova
transcript.text: I'll deliver the high-fidelity mockups for the import modal and template selector by Wednesday afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Perfect. Let's aim for a full QA release candidate by end of next week. Thanks all!

analysis.executiveSummary: The team aligned on the H2 AI meeting intelligence strategy, confirming low-latency infrastructure on Neon PostgreSQL, cost-effective LLM extraction using GPT-4o Mini, and an executive-first AI Review audit interface. Key milestones were assigned for prompt engineering, JSON import/export, and UX designs.
keyTakeaways: Sub-50ms search latency achieved on Neon PostgreSQL serverless architecture.
GPT-4o Mini selected as default model delivering 92% cost savings with high audit fidelity.
User research highlighted high demand for AI Readiness Scores and click-to-seek playback sync.
Targeting end of next week for full QA release candidate.

meetings.title: Q3 Product Launch Sync & Risk Assessment

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Good morning everyone. We have exactly 72 hours until our Q3 launch. Let's do a fast go/no-go assessment across frontend performance, rate limiting, and marketing enablement.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: On the client side, the meeting player and synchronized transcript highlights are locked. We tested latency with 50+ participants and client memory stayed rock-solid under 45MB.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: That's exceptional news. Marcus, how are backend rate limits and LLM inference costs looking?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Brody
transcript.text: We noticed a spike when power users trigger three summaries in under a minute. To protect latency, I recommend introducing a Redis token-bucket rate limiter and setting a BYOK Bring-Your-Own-Key model for heavy enterprise accounts.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Agreed. Let's make BYOK standard for heavy usage while giving free users 5 full runs a day. Marcus, can you get that implemented and tested before Thursday staging freeze?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Brody
transcript.text: Yes, I will have the PR merged by Thursday noon.

transcript.speaker: Elena Rostova
transcript.text: From the marketing side, the changelog draft and customer announcement emails are ready. But we need deep-link timestamps in all copied markdown exports so customers can click directly back to the audio moment.

transcript.speaker: Alex Rivera
transcript.text: I can add ?t=seconds deep links to our markdown export helper today. It's a quick 30-minute win.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Perfect. So all clipboard exports will contain deep-linked transcript timestamps by default. Let's lock staging for Thursday night and launch Friday at 2 PM EST.

analysis.executiveSummary: The product and engineering teams completed a final pre-launch readiness review for the Q3 release. Frontend latency and memory metrics passed benchmark tests under high load. To mitigate LLM cost overhead, the team adopted a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) architecture alongside token-bucket throttling. Export workflows were enhanced with transcript deep links, and the launch target was locked for Friday at 2 PM EST.
keyTakeaways: Frontend synchronized transcript player achieved stable performance under 45MB RAM.
Adopted Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) tiering alongside Redis rate limiting for AI queries.
All clipboard and markdown exports will include source timestamp deep links.
Staging lock confirmed for Thursday night with public announcement Friday at 2 PM EST.

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Hi David, Rachel, great to connect. Today we wanted to understand Acme's current meeting transcription bottlenecks and evaluate how Fathom can streamline your executive reporting.

transcript.speaker: David Miller
transcript.text: Our primary headache is meeting sprawl across 300 engineers. Team leads spend 4 hours a week writing meeting minutes and half the action items get lost in Slack channels.

transcript.speaker: Rachel Zane
transcript.text: Security is our biggest blocker. We cannot have transcript data trained on by foundational model providers. Does Fathom offer zero-data retention agreements with OpenAI?

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. We support enterprise zero-data retention (ZDR) and Bring-Your-Own-Key so queries bypass our servers directly to your private enterprise tenant.

transcript.speaker: David Miller
transcript.text: That is huge for our InfoSec approval. If we can run a 50-seat pilot starting next month, what would the pricing structure look like?

transcript.speaker: Sarah Chen
transcript.text: I will prepare a custom proposal covering a 50-seat pilot with dedicated onboarding and SOC2 compliance addendum by Wednesday.

analysis.executiveSummary: Acme Corp is evaluating Fathom AI to solve meeting sprawl across their 300-person engineering organization. Key evaluation criteria include zero-data retention (ZDR), Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) privacy controls, and automated action item syncing. Acme is ready to proceed with a 50-seat pilot pending InfoSec review.
keyTakeaways: Acme engineers spend 4 hours/week manually summarizing meetings with frequent lost action items.
Zero-data retention (ZDR) and BYOK LLM options satisfy Acme's security prerequisites.
David requested a 50-seat pilot proposal starting next month.
